Rims located by hand by the user in data/labeling/rim_wide/label.html, two clicks per ring, plus frames confirmed to hold no rim.

WIDTHS WERE CORRECTED, and the reason is a fault in my instructions rather than in the labelling. 'The leftmost point of the orange ring' is ambiguous between the ring's outer extent and the opening it encircles, and the two labellers read it differently. Measured on 34 rings we both labelled within 2 s:
    centres agree to 0.12 rim widths (median) -- the gate's tolerance is 1.0
    widths differ by a factor of 0.70 (median), systematically
So the POSITIONS, which are the judgement and the hard part, agree closely. Only the size convention differed.

The correction is size-banded because a single factor does not fit: x1.5 was rendered over the rings and lands exactly on the outer edge for rings under ~120 px (15->22, 18->27, 30->45, 49->74 all checked), while on close-ups it overshoots badly (531->799 spills well past the ring). Rings at or above 120 px are therefore left as labelled; they sit within ~0.8 of mine, inside the tolerance that matters.

An automatic alternative was tried and rejected: snapping each width to the orange blob at the click. It brought the two labellers' median agreement to 1.00 but merged the ring with the backboard's red padding on distant rims (12 -> 46) and occasionally seized the wrong component (486 -> 1122).
